key_insight: Automatic-differentiation reveals that aerodynamic information from sparse pressure sensors is transported unevenly through compressible flow, creating localized high-observability regions that help but do not fully determine inverse learning success.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for choosing sensor locations and assessing parameter identifiability in compressible aerodynamics, especially for inverse design and flow reconstruction.
method: Backpropagate through the full unsteady flow to compute observability from sparse pressure measurements
Use the metric to compare sensor locations and parameter-recovery performance
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inverse-learning experiments showing that highly observable probes usually improve recovery, but the highest-observability probe is not always the best for inference, and results vary with flow regime and airfoil geometry.
watch_item: Observability is not identical to learnability, so sensor rankings from the metric may not directly translate to best inverse-learning performance in every case.
paper_title: Information Transport and Observability in Compressible Aerodynamics
